chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
I asked him about the slave (male or female), how many is permissible for him to marry? He said: 'Two free women or four slave women.'
And he said: 'There is no harm if he has wealth in his hand and is permitted in trade, that he may buy whatever he wishes of the slave women and have relations with them.'
As for the free women, it is not permissible for him to contract marriage with more than two of them, according to what we have previously mentioned.
And to emphasize this clarification, also, is what has been narrated:

key_terms.يَطَأَهُنَّ: To have relations with them (consummate marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum number of wives a slave can marry according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the marital capacity of a *mamluk* (male slave), permitting him to marry up to two free women or four slave women, contingent upon possessing independent wealth and trade permission. It highlights the jurisprudential distinction between the fixed limit of two free wives and the flexibility to acquire additional slave wives through personal earnings, reflecting the socio-economic realities of slavery in early Shia legal theory. The hadith underscores the concept of *mudabbir* or financially independent slaves who could manage their own affairs, including marriage contracts, within the bounds of their master's authority.
